items.title: PlanetScale now offers dedicated read replicas for Postgres
items.blurb: Use dedicated read replicas to isolate read-only workloads and distribute your data across data centers around the world.

items.title: Heroku Postgres Advanced is now generally available
items.blurb: Heroku Postgres Advanced is now available. Our new database tier brings decoupled storage, 3x–4x throughput, instance pools, and non-disruptive operations.

items.title: 'PlanetScale Released Text Search and We Have a Lot to Say'
items.blurb: Two BM25 optimizations and benchmark configuration changes inspired by PlanetScale's TIN benchmarks make ParadeDB's text search faster without changing its document identifiers.

items.title: Running Apache Cloudberry as Postgres Extensions
items.blurb: A personal experiment: Apache Cloudberry, the most up-to-date open-source version of Greenplum, turned into a set of extensions for PostgreSQL 19.

items.title: Upgrading a 56TB Database by Mostly Not Moving It
items.blurb: We had to upgrade our 56TB Aurora Postgres cluster by 31 July without taking Trigger.dev down. Instead of moving the database, we made the problem smaller: new runs and the control plane went to PlanetScale, and the old runs stayed behind.
